title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these notes return to the 1966 Tate letter programme, a Dieudonné theory for finite group schemes in characteristic p. The previous page proves Witt-vector lemmas for a subgroup H of G_a that is locally of the form 'kernel of an additive (Frobenius-type) polynomial', i.e. G_a/H is locally isomorphic to G_a. Two statements come from there: Ext^1(H,W_n) -> Ext^1(H,W_1) is bijective, and the transition maps V: Ext^1(H,W_{n-1}) -> Ext^1(H,W_n) are zero.

Corollary 3. Let W = lim_{->} W_n, with transition maps V. This is the ind-group of 'unipotent Witt covectors' (Fontaine's CW^u). The sheaf Ext^1(H, W) vanishes, since a filtered colimit of groups along zero maps is zero.

Question. Does the global Ext^1(H,W) vanish too? Given the corollary, global Ext^1 equals H^1(S, Hom(H,W)) by the local-to-global spectral sequence. Grothendieck answers 'No, already for H = alpha_p, e.g. S = Spec k with k imperfect.' The marginal reason is illegible.

Proposition 4. Let G be a finite algebraic group over a field k of characteristic p, not necessarily perfect, killed by V^n, of rank p^r. Then:
(a) Hom_gr(G, W_n) is a smooth group scheme (connected?) of dimension r, 'isomorphic to E^r_k' in a struck-out version, presumably vector-group-like.
(b) The sheaf Ext^1_gr(G, W) vanishes.

Proof. (b) follows by dévissage of G into copies of alpha_p, using Cor. 3 and the long exact Ext sequence. For (a), induct on the length of a composition series 0 -> G' -> G -> alpha_p -> 0. Since Ext^1(alpha_p, W) = 0 one gets
0 -> Hom(alpha_p, W) -> Hom(G, W) -> Hom(G', W) -> 0,
then passes from W to W_n. Since Hom(alpha_p, W_n) ≅ G_a and Hom(G', W_n) is smooth by induction, Hom(G, W_n) is an extension of smooth groups, hence smooth ('On gagne!').

§5. Define D(G) = Hom(G, W). It is a W_∞-module (W_∞ = p-typical Witt vectors of the base), with F and V induced from those on W. They satisfy (5.1): F lambda = lambda^sigma F, lambda V = V lambda^sigma, FV = VF = p. This is the contravariant Witt-covector Dieudonné module, defined here over an arbitrary base of characteristic p, including imperfect fields.

The next page switches to the crystalline construction D_*(G), D^*(G), starting with étale groups and truncated Barsotti–Tate groups. So this page is the 'Witt-covector side' of a planned comparison between the classical and crystalline Dieudonné functors over non-perfect bases.
errors: The dévissage 'G se dévisse en groupes isomorphes à alpha_p' holds only for infinitesimal unipotent G (killed by F^m and V^n). A finite group killed by V^n can have an étale part: the constant group Z/p has V = 0. Over an imperfect field there are also étale and non-trivial twisted forms. These need separate treatment (e.g. Ext^1(Z/p, W) = W/pW, which needs divisibility of W) or an explicit infinitesimality hypothesis.

If the hypothesis were weakened to 'killed by V^m' with m > n, (a) would fail. For example Hom(Z/p, W_2) = W_2[p] ≅ alpha_p × G_a as a scheme, which is not smooth. The statement correctly ties the exponent n of V^n to W_n, but this point is worth noting.

The 'Non' to the global question is asserted without a visible argument. Given Cor. 3 and Hom(alpha_p, W) being (a colimit of) G_a over a field, it is not obvious why H^1 is nonzero. The intended base or topology (perhaps a non-reduced S, or an étale vs fppf issue) is unclear from the page, so the claim cannot be checked as stated.
In (5.1) the relation written as 'lambda V = V lambda^p' should read lambda V = V lambda^sigma (sigma = Witt Frobenius). This is presumably only notation.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the Witt-covector Dieudonné functor D(G) = Hom(G, W) over a non-perfect base, intended for comparison with the crystalline D^*(G) on the next page. This page stops at the axioms (5.1), and the comparison is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Soit D(G)=Hom(G,W). C'est un W_∞-Module, muni des endom. V et F satisfaisant les conditions habituelles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The comparison between Witt-covector and crystalline Dieudonné modules over imperfect or non-perfect bases was later done in pieces (Berthelot–Breen–Messing, Zink, Lau). This shows Grothendieck planned it in the same notes, but the content is largely subsumed by later work.

missed.claim: Smoothness of Hom_gr(G, W_n), of dimension log_p rank G, for (infinitesimal) unipotent G killed by V^n over an imperfect field, by an explicit alpha_p-dévissage.
missed.quote: Hom_gr(G,W_n) est un schéma en groupes lisse ... rg G = p^r
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest concrete lemma. I am unsure whether it is stated in this form for imperfect fields in Demazure–Gabriel or later. It is of minor interest for unipotent group schemes over imperfect fields.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard Witt-covector computations in the style of Demazure–Gabriel, extended to imperfect fields. They are interesting as a record of Grothendieck's planned non-perfect Dieudonné theory, but the content is largely known and has a small gap (the étale part is missing from the dévissage).
transcription_corrections: 'il procède par récurrence' should read 'on procède par récurrence'.
In the exact sequence, the middle and right terms are Hom(G, W) and Hom(G', W), with W underlined with an arrow (the colimit), not W_n. The subsequent replacement by W_n is described in words.
(5.1) 'lambda V = V lambda^p' is most likely lambda V = V lambda^sigma (Frobenius on W_∞).
The struck-out passage in Prop. 4(a) reads approximately '(et isomorphe à E^r_k si r = ... ; rg G = p^r)'. Only 'rg G = p^r' survives unstruck.
